newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end weaker in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end weaker in quiet trading.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker in quiet trade on Monday, with many players taking profits on last week's gains amid a lack of significant news or data, analysts said.

"We've reached I think a point to some extent of technical tiredness in the market here. Rates have pushed ahead by so much," said Jim Webber, director of fixed-income research with TD Securities. "A little bit of a pullback like this doesn't really imply much."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.47 to C$118.50 to yield 6.577 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 10/32 to yield 6.55 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to three basis points from two basis points at Friday's close.

Canadian and U.S. bond markets saw light activity, with many traders focused on economic data out later in the week. Key Canadian economic reports out this week include the consumer price index for June out on Thursday and merchandise and wholesale trade data for May on Friday.
Analysts said concern about U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on July 22 had begun to affect trading.
"People are looking at Humphrey-Hawkins and waiting to see what kind of message Greenspan has at that point," said Webber.

In corporate debt news, Oxford Properties Group Inc said it would issue C$100 million of 6.86 percent debentures due 2004 with CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Inc and Nesbitt Burns Inc co-leading the underwriting.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.33 to C$109.12 to yield 6.011 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond fell 7/32 to yield 6.25 percent.
The negative spread between the two benchmark bonds was 24 basis points, unchanged from Friday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.17 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.14 percent.
